model_definitions.B_optimizer_only: complete stepwise AdamW tangent; pulse delta_g=q then future delta_g=0 [FR_A0C]
model_definitions.C_full_tangent: complete stepwise AdamW tangent; future delta_g=clip_jvp(H(loss)*delta_theta) [FR_A0C]

conclusions.c_vs_b_explanation: Paired per-state comparison over 32 sampled states and horizons H=1,2,4,8: C beats B in 96/128 rows (ties 32, losses 0); mean relative-error improvement +0.124154, median +0.0441067, worst regression +0. H=1 rows are a zero-control (B == C by construction, no future step).
conclusions.consistency_explanation: Mean B-to-C relative-error improvement is positive on 3/4 horizons and on 8/8 seeds. Mean relative error over all rows: A=4.52298, B=0.128616, C=0.0044613.
conclusions.ordering_explanation: Ordering is by mean relative error over all sampled state-horizon rows; no fitted or empirical variable enters any model.
conclusions.recommended_next_step: If uniformly favorable, extend the same frozen A/B/C comparison to the full 56-state v07 bank and to the v06 replication bank for cross-partition generalization; do not fit any memory kernel before that.
conclusions.further_question: Are the B-beating-C state-horizon rows explained by active clipping at the registered epsilon (see A0E decomposition) rather than by missing smooth curvature?
